SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT
（批：8/24 31 9 III）
O.S.S. Special Branch Station. File No.................... Date September 9, 1941.
SUBJECT: Increase of price of foreign lodging house registers.
I beg to report having been informed, on September 8th. 1941, by Supt. MacFarlane, Quartermaster, that the price of foreign lodging house registers has been increased, as from this month, from $4.50 to $18.00 per register.
In this connection I wish to state, that the majority of foreign lodging house proprietors located North of the Soochow Creek, are German Jewish refugees and poorer class Russians and that the present increase of the existing price by 300% will, undoubtedly, impede the sale of registers. Even at the price of registers at $4.50 per book, difficulties have been experienced by members of staff attached to this Section to induce lodging house owners to acquire the necessary registers, the maintenance of which by the said owners is indispensable for the efficient control of lodgers by the Police.
In order to compare the periodical increase of the price of registers, I beg to submit the following data, recorded in this Office, of the sale of Registers to owners of lodging houses:-
Between 1937 and April 1939 ............ $1.50
" April 1939 and November 1939 ....... $1.50
" November 1939 and November 1940 ... $2.50
" Nov. 1940 and up to the present ... $4.50
Should the licence fee of a 3-4 roomed foreign lodging house which, at the present time, is $13.50 per half a year, also be taken into consideration, the price of a register in comparison to that of the licence fee seems to be well out of proportion.
Furthermore, condition No.10 of the foreign
pages.zh:

报告
（批：8/24 31 9 III）
O.S.S. 特别分部 警署。档案号.................... 日期 1941年9月9日。
主题：外侨寄宿公寓登记簿价格上涨。
谨此报告，我于1941年9月8日接到军需官 MacFarlane 督察的通知，外侨寄宿公寓登记簿的价格自本月起已从每本4.50美元上涨至18.00美元。
在此方面，我想指出，位于苏州河北岸的大多数外侨寄宿公寓业主是德籍犹太难民和较贫困阶层的俄国人，目前价格大幅上涨300%，无疑将阻碍登记簿的销售。即使登记簿价格为每本4.50美元时，本部门的工作人员在促使寄宿公寓业主购买必要的登记簿方面也遇到了困难，而这些业主维持登记簿对于警方有效管控住客至关重要。
为了比较登记簿价格的定期上涨情况，谨提交本办公室记录的向寄宿公寓业主销售登记簿的以下数据：-
1937年至1939年4月 ............ 1.50美元
" 1939年4月至1939年11月 ....... 1.50美元
" 1939年11月至1940年11月 ... 2.50美元
" 1940年11月至今 ... 4.50美元
如果考虑到拥有3-4个房间的外侨寄宿公寓目前的执照费为每半年13.50美元，那么登记簿的价格与执照费相比似乎极不成比例。
此外，外侨

“持照人须在经营场所内保存一份永久、准确且字迹清晰的登记簿，记录所有光顾或使用该场所人员的姓名、国籍、职业、工作地点、前住址、目的地以及抵达和离开日期，该登记簿须随时供工部局警务处或其他经正式授权的工部局官员检查 ...........”

Made by... D.S.I. Wittinsky... Forwarded by... Supt. Mason.

In accordance with verbal instructions
received from Supt. Mason, P.A. to D.C. (Special Branch),
I beg to apply for a substitute to fill in the vacancy
on the staff of C.S.6 following the retirement of
D.S.I. Medvedeff from the S.M.Police on the 10-10-40.
I beg to report that in addition to the regular supervi-
sion of some 226 licenced Lodging Houses, 86 licensed
Private Hotels and some 40 unlicensed lodging houses,
the foreign members of C.S.6 are performing duties in
connection with the following:- Enquiries re applications
for licences, movements and activities of criminals and
suspects, translation and examination of printed matter
pertaining to documents, plays, scripts of songs,
dialogue sheets etc. in the German language; attendance
for the purpose of supervision and censorship of
theatres, cabarets, meetings and various religious
services held in the Northern district; general enquiries
on behalf of Police Stations including the French
Police and censorship of Chinese Newspapers.

under supervision are presently sub-divided into three
districts; two are located North of the Soochow Creek
covering the Hongkew, Wayside and Yulin Road Police
Districts, and one South of the Soochow Creek including
the Central, Chengtu, Sinza, Bubbling Well Road and
Gordon Road Police Districts. With reference to
supervision of boarding houses in the Northern District,
I beg to report that the foreign staff of this Section

Your obedient servant,

where licensees were prosecuted after two such notifications had been ignored.

D. C. (Special Branch)
Sir,

Staff of Boarding House Section.

There has been a decided increase in the boarding and lodging houses operating North of the Soochow Creek. The number previously was 96, mostly in the Hongkew and Wayside Districts, but in the last year has increased to 156 and further applications are received daily. A number of these premises are now located in the Kashing Road and Yulin Road District, even to the borders of Yangtsepoo maintain District and in order to keep a proper check and proper supervision, a visit is made each one twice a month, and it is well nigh impossible for one man to do this, transportation being a difficult problem in the area concerned.

The staff of the Boarding House Section, C.S.S. is composed of D.S.I. Wittinsky in charge, who also deals with German refugee applications for licences; D.S.I. Medvedeff, supervision of foreign boarding and lodging houses (87) on the South side of the Soochow Creek, and general inquiries into licences also South of the Creek. D.S. Cornwell is responsible for the shipping lists and enquiries and at the present time this is a long job, as under present conditions, brought about by the European war, shipping companies do not issue copies of passenger lists and they have to be examined and if necessary copied in the shipping offices which requires constant visits, no arrival dates being published.

D.S. Mischenko is at present visiting the premises located in the Northern and Eastern districts necessitating his staying down there the whole day and having to purchase his food. Bus passes on the Japanese controlled buses are

致：副总监（特别处）
先生：

寄宿房屋科人员编制。

苏州河以北运营的寄宿和 lodging 房屋数量显著增加。此前数量为96家，主要分布在虹口和韦尔斯区（Wayside District），但在过去一年中已增至156家，且每日仍有新的申请递交。其中许多场所现在位于嘉善路（Kashing Road）和榆林路（Yulin Road）区域，甚至延伸至杨树浦维持区（Yangtsepoo maintain District）的边缘。为了保持适当的核查与监管，每家每月需走访两次，鉴于该区域交通困难，一人几乎无法完成此项工作。

刑事调查处（C.S.S.）寄宿房屋科的人员构成如下：由警司维廷斯基（D.S.I. Wittinsky）负责，他还处理德国难民执照申请；警司梅德韦杰夫（D.S.I. Medvedeff），负责监管苏州河南岸的外国寄宿和 lodging 房屋（87家），并负责南岸的一般执照查询。警佐康威尔（D.S. Cornwell）负责船运名单及查询，目前这是一项耗时的工作，因为在欧洲战争造成的当前局势下，轮船公司不签发乘客名单副本，必须前往轮船公司办公室查阅，必要时进行抄录，这需要频繁走访，因为抵达日期并未公布。

警佐米申科（D.S. Mischenko）目前正在走访位于北部和东部区域的场所，这使他不得不整日停留在那里并自行购买食物。在日本控制的公共汽车上使用的月票价格为

pages.en:

issued monthly at Y.5.50 ($7.70) but these passes
are only good on buses plying in certain districts,
i.e. the buses operating in Hongkew, Dixwell Road and
Kashing Road, one pass, Wayside and Yulin Road, one pass,
Yangtsepoо, one pass, making a total of $23.10 every month.

In view of the conditions prevailing and the
inadvisability of one man attempting to supervise so many
houses and the daily increase of such premises, I would
respectfully suggest that another detective be appointed
to the boarding house section preferably one of Russian
nationality with a knowledge of the German language.
The Eastern District could then be divided between two
men and transportation to the districts concerned could
be arranged with the office car.

Indian Section.

In the past month we have had many calls for
the services of Indian detectives and with only four
detectives available it has been a bit difficult. Also
the movement among Indians of an anti-British tendency
has shown a decided strengthening, especially in the area
North of the Soochow Creek and is being abetted by Japanese
interests. The German propaganda machine in Shanghai has
also shown a tendency to play up this attitude of the
Indians and which has not been lost on the Indian community.

With the present staff it is not possible to cover
this adequately and I would recommend the appointment of
another Indian constable to the staff for the purpose of
keeping in touch with those being exploited by the Japanese.

C. Crawford

P.A.to D.C.(Sp.Br.)

印度人科。

在过去的一个月里，我们对印度侦探的需求很多，
而仅有四名侦探可用，因此略显困难。此外，印度人中
反英倾向的运动显示出明显的加强，特别是在苏州河
以北地区，并受到日本势力的煽动。上海的德国宣传
机器也表现出利用印度人这种态度的倾向，这一点已
被印度社群所察觉。

以现有人员无法充分覆盖这一领域，我建议向该科
增派一名印度巡捕，以便与被日本人利用的那些人
保持联系。

C. 克劳福德

men and transportation to the districts concerned could
be arranged with the office car.

Indian Section.

In the past month we have had many calls for
the services of Indian detectives and with only four
detectives available it has been a bit difficult. Also
the movement among Indians of an anti-British tendency
has shown a decided strengthening, especially in the area
North of the Soochow Creek and is being abetted by Japanese
interests. The German propaganda machine in Shanghai has
also shown a tendency to play up this attitude of the
Indians and which has not been lost on the Indian community.

With the present staff it is not possible to cover
this adequately and I would recommend the appointment of
another Indian constable to the staff for the purpose of
keeping in touch with these being exploited by the Japanese.

P.A.to D.C.(Sp.Br.)

Date December 5, 1939.
No. 8/24
Date 6 / 12 39

D.C.(Special Branch)
Sir,

Foreign Criminals and Suspects.

At the present time there is only one Station
submitting copies of reports on foreigners arrested for
criminal cases and that is Hongkew. The other day,
November 28th, 1939, D.S.I. Wittinsky on a visit to the
Eastern District on lodging house applications, picked
up a Russian woman wanted by Bubbling Well Station for
larceny, and this detective who is in charge of the
Boarding-House Section only knew of this woman being wanted
through a casual conversation with Bubbling Well detectives.
D.S. Mischenko also arrested a well known pickpocket in the
Yokohama Specie Bank on December 4th, 1939. Records are
kept of all known foreigners, suspects and criminals, by
C.S.6 Boarding-House Section, and I think that most of the
detectives attached to Stations are not aware of this.
There have been times when we have been able to assist those
who do make use of such a valuable source of information and
in order to keep this record up to scratch I would suggest
with your permission that I make arrangements with
P.A. (Crime) to have all cases forwarded to Special Branch
from Crime Branch Registry thereby relieving the Stations
of extra work in submitting copies.

FILE

C. Crawford
P.A. to D.C. (Sp.Br.)

same company, the "Messageries Maritimes", but it would
appear a temporary arrangement was made through the
good offices of Chief Inspector Emelianoff of the
French Police which has not been at all satisfactory.

reluctance to give copies or even show the passenger

importance to that Section for the purpose of keeping

letter be despatched to the managers of the shipping

Subject......... Request of Messrs. Messageries Maritimes.
Made by ............ and ................ Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

D.S. Hocking reports that on the occasion of
his last visit, May 26, of the offices of Messrs. Messageries
Maritimes, the manager stated that in looking over his files
he could not find any letter from the Municipal Police
requesting for delivery of passenger lists. This being the
case, he would suggest that a formal request be addressed to
his company for purposes of record.

In view of the fact that many other foreign
shipping agencies have made similar suggestions to representa-
tives of the Police, I beg to suggest that formal requests be
made to them on lines as submitted in the attached draft.

Such a request would not obligate the Municipal
Police in any way at the same time it would facilitate co-
operation and also strengthen the hands of the local agencies
vis-a-vis their home offices.

E. Papp
Inspector.

Adjustment of work between C. 2 and C. S. 6.

/ and Inspector Pegg.

Acting in accordance with instructions contained
in the attached memorandum from D. C. (Special Branch), I most
respectfully beg to submit for approval the following proposals,
which have been worked out in co-operation with and complete
agreement of P. A. (Crime) and D. S. I. Dickson with a view to
eradicating unnecessary duplication of work between C. 2 and
C. S. 6:-

(1). C. 2 would henceforth keep the Force informed regarding
the arrests of foreign criminals, (if considered of
sufficient importance) through Daily Information Sheet,
immediately after being charged or sentenced; thus
eliminating the necessity of publishing the monthly lists
of known criminals, which was prepared by C. S. 6.

(2). As it has already comprehensive records of all known
criminals, C. 2 would provide C. S. 6, with the names of all
criminals arrested together with C. R. O. numbers etc. to
enable the latter Section to maintain an efficient
surveillance on the movements of criminals and their
associates. In this connection it is suggested that the
attached forms be adopted to facilitate exchange of
information between the two Sections. Form "A" to be used
by C. 2 to inform C. S. 6 of the arrests of foreigners while
Form "B" to be used by C. S. 6 to inform C. 2 and C/S of the
movements of known criminals.

(3) In distinction to C. 2, which keeps a record of all known
criminals, C. S. 6 would collect and record information on
the activities and movements of persons suspected to be
engaged in criminal activities and also of suspects of
a political nature.

C. 2股与 C. S. 6股之间的工作调整。

/ 和佩格（Pegg）督察。

根据附上的特别处副总监备忘录中的指示，我谨恭敬地提交以下提案以供批准，这些提案是与犯罪科助理员（P. A. (Crime)）和迪克森（Dickson）副督察合作并在完全达成一致的情况下制定的，旨在消除C. 2股与C. S. 6股之间不必要的工作重复：-

(1). C. 2股今后将通过《每日情报表》（Daily Information Sheet），在外国人犯被起诉或判刑后立即通知本警队关于逮捕外国罪犯的情况（如果认为足够重要）；从而消除了发布由C. S. 6股编制的已知罪犯月度名单的必要。

(2). 由于C. 2股已经拥有所有已知罪犯的综合记录，C. 2股将向C. S. 6股提供所有被捕罪犯的姓名以及刑事登记处（C. R. O.）号码等，以便后者该股能够对罪犯及其同伙的行踪保持有效的监视。在这方面，建议采用所附表格以促进两股之间的信息交换。“A”表由C. 2股用于通知C. S. 6股关于外国人的逮捕情况，而“B”表由C. S. 6股用于通知C. 2股和各警署（C/S）关于已知罪犯的行踪。

(3) 与记录所有已知罪犯的C. 2股不同，C. S. 6股将收集和记录涉嫌从事犯罪活动的人员以及具有政治性质的嫌疑人的活动和行踪信息。

Date...January..12,..19 37.
Subject ..C.S.6. - Data on Foreign criminals and suspects. - Guide cards used in....
connection with index thereof - necessity for renewal and expansion.
Made by................and................Forwarded by...........D.S.I. Golder.

The index of Criminals and Criminal-suspects as originally
introduced in 1934 for use in connection with the revised acti-
vities of Section C.S.6 has become obsolete by reason of the
fact that the total number of references has expanded threefold
in the past year and half, reaching a total of 5,500 direct
references.

Briefly the original idea was to use a two way numerical
index, one on a series of cards at the front of each draw
showing the number of the card bearing the particulars of the
person regarding whom reference was being made and the other
a non-recurring serial number common only to the section.

The use of these two systems led in time to untold confu-
sion in the matter of quoting the numerical indicators of
criminals and suspects, it was for this reason abandoned and
all convicted criminals referred to by their Crime Record Office
numbers, as maintained by the Finger Print Bureau. In this
matter the Finger Print Bureau have been of the greatest
assistance.

As to suspects, it has been proved inadvisable to refer
to them under a number since such would have to be abandoned
as soon as they were charged and convicted. Thus suspects,
except those with International records, the particulars of
whom are on file with the Finger Print Bureau, are merely
referred to in the files of the section under their names.

When it was found necessary to drop the old system and
recourse was made to the Finger Print Bureau for the definite
identification of the hundreds of persons on the sections files
it was discovered that such only covered a fraction of the
work to be taken in if the work was to be of any value to the

日期……1937年1月12日。
主题……C.S.6. - 关于外籍罪犯及嫌疑人的资料。- 与此索引相关的指引卡片 - 更新与扩充的必要性。
制作者………………及………………呈送者………副督察长 Golder。

最初于1934年引入、供C.S.6股修订后的活动使用的罪犯及犯罪嫌疑人索引，因在过去一年半中引用总数扩大了三倍，达到直接引用总数5,500条，而已变得过时。

简而言之，最初的想法是使用一种双向数字索引，一种位于每个抽屉前部的一系列卡片上，显示载有被查询人详情的卡片编号，另一种则是仅该股通用的不重复序列号。

随着时间推移，使用这两套系统在引用罪犯和嫌疑人的数字标识时导致了无数的混乱，因此被放弃，所有已定罪罪犯均参照指纹局维护的犯罪记录办公室（Crime Record Office）编号进行指代。在此事项上，指纹局提供了极大的协助。

至于嫌疑人，事实证明不宜用编号指代他们，因为一旦他们被起诉并定罪，该编号就必须废弃。因此，除拥有国际记录且其详情存档于指纹局的嫌疑人外，该股档案中仅以其姓名指代嫌疑人。

当发现有必要弃用旧系统并求助于指纹局以明确识别该股档案中的数百人时，人们发现，如果这项工作要对警队

Force. Duplications were rife and omissions present in plenty,
largely owing to the fact that there was no point of reference
between the old Boarding House Section "Serial Number" and the
reference numbers in use by the Finger-print Bureau. This state
of affairs has to a great extent been removed; the sections
index now being complete in accordance with the Crime Record
Office reference numbers up to October 1936. Since that date
some three hundred persons have appeared either as fresh cri-
minals and as a consequence been placed on the C.R.O. list or
have been brought forward from the old Finger Print Bureau
reference system. By the time the C.R.O. is complete some
5,500 persons will appear in its files. They will include
dilinquents in every phase of crime.
It will be readily appreciated that it would be difficult
for the staff of this Section to maintain an efficient surveil-
lance on the movements of criminals and their associates through
their routine work unless the names of such persons are on file
with the Section. It would be tantamount to looking for a
needle in a hay stack, whilst blindfolded.
The method now adopted is effective, yet unobstrusive, and
devised to give no possible cause for complaint on the part of
the persons under surveillance. In point of fact it invariably
happens that all the enquiries necessary for the positive
identification of a person can be carried out in the Headquarters
building once a pointer has been obtained.
I have attached herewith a suggestion for the re-indexing
of the criminal and suspect cards, which beside meeting present
requirements, allows for future expansion: the cost would be
under $20.00.

有任何价值，这仅仅涵盖了所需开展工作的一小部分。重复现象普遍存在，遗漏也大量存在，这很大程度上是因为旧的寄宿房屋股“序列号”与指纹局使用的参考编号之间没有参照点。这种情况已在很大程度上得到消除；该股的索引现在根据截至1936年10月的犯罪记录办公室参考编号完整编制。自该日期以来，约有三百人作为新罪犯出现，因而被列入犯罪记录办公室名单，或从旧的指纹局参考系统中调出。待犯罪记录办公室工作完成时，其档案中将出现约5,500人。他们将包括各个犯罪阶段的不法分子。
显而易见，除非这些人的姓名存档于该股，否则该股职员很难通过日常工作对罪犯及其同伙的行踪保持有效的监视。这无异于蒙着眼睛在干草堆里找针。
目前采用的方法既有效又不引人注目，旨在不给被监视人员任何可能的投诉理由。事实上，一旦获得线索，所有用于确证某人身份的必要查询 invariably（总是）可以在总部大楼内完成。
随函附上关于重新编制罪犯和嫌疑人卡片索引的建议，该建议除了满足当前需求外，还为未来的扩展留有余地：费用将在20.00美元以下。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
C.S.6, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. S. B. D. 8/34
14 / 2 36
Date Dec. 10. 36.
Subject Visitors to Convicts in the Ward Road Gaol --- Record for Information
Purposes to be Filed with C. S. 6. --- Suggestion.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Golder.

During the past year there have been numerous
instances wherein useful information regarding the true
addresses of convicts, and other material of vital importance
as Police intelligence, has been obtained from the record of
visitors to convicts in the Ward Road Gaol. In one instance
the arrest of a wanted man was brought about by a careful
scrutiny of the names of the persons visiting him during a
previous term of imprisonment. At the home of one of his
visitors the wanted man was located and arrested.
It is not proposed to make immediate or pointed
enquiries into the bonafides of the visitors to convicts
but to include their names and addresses on the reference
cards of convicted persons filed in this Section so that
at any future date, should it arise that an ex-convict is
wanted for further offences, the investigating officer has
at least something to work on.
To enable the Gaol Staff to assist in this
matter, I have designed a form (draft attached) to be filled
in and thereafter forwarded to this Section for disposal.
It would greatly help this Section's work if the completed
forms could be sent in weekly.

Governor of Gaols
Very grateful if you will comply
provided there is no objection from your
side of Gaol
D. C. Special Branch.
Ken Golder
D. S. I.
DEPUTY COMMISSIONER
(SPECIAL BRANCH)
11 DEC. 1936

主题 华德路监狱罪犯访客 --- 供参考的记录存于 C. S. 6。--- 建议。
制作者及呈送者 副督察长 Golder。

在过去一年中，有许多实例表明，通过华德路监狱罪犯访客记录，获得了关于罪犯真实地址的有用信息，以及作为警方情报至关重要的其他材料。在一个案例中，通过对一名通缉犯在前次服刑期间访客姓名的仔细审查，促成了对该人的逮捕。在该通缉犯的一名访客家中，找到了此人并将其逮捕。
拟议并非立即或直接调查罪犯访客的真实性，而是将他们的姓名和地址列入存于本股的已定罪人员参考卡片中，以便将来若某前科犯因进一步犯罪而被通缉时，调查官员至少有一些线索可循。
为使监狱职员能在此事上提供协助，我设计了一份表格（草案附后），填写后 forwarded 至本股处理。如果能每周发送填妥的表格，将极大地帮助本股的工作。

监狱典狱长
如果您那边监狱方面没有异议，
恳请配合，不胜感激
副 commissioner （特务科）。
Ken Golder

Acting in accordance with the instructions of the
Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch) an interview was obtained
with Dr. Hong Chi, Chief of the 2nd Division, Bureau of Public
Safety on October 22. 1936.
The matter of the surveillance maintained on the movements
of foreign criminals and undesirables was explained to Dr. Hong
Chi, who promised to write to the Chinese shipping concerns
operating ships along the China Coast, requesting that they supply
the information desired.
For the time being particulars of foreign passengers will
be sent to Dr. Hong Chi, and will thereafter be transmitted
to the Shanghai Municipal Police. Should the data prove of
value it will eventually be arranged by Dr. Hong Chi that the
companies address the S.M.P. direct.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No: ... 1). 8/24
C.S.6. Special Branch. ... /10 36
REPORT.
Date October 21. .. 36.

Subject Passenger lists - Arrivals and Departures.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Golder.

The system of putting up the names of incoming and
outgoing passengers alphabetically in the files of Section
'C.S.6., as introduced from January 1936, has proved of the
greatest benefit to all those called upon to trace the
arrivals and departures of foreign nationals. Once a name
is obtained, reference can be made in under one minute, the
entry giving the name of the passenger, name of the ship
and the date of its arrival or departure.

In the manner described above much valuable information
may be obtained especially concerning arrivals, without
approaching outside persons, consulates or commercial
concerns. Thus the system has two salient features (1)
that it is more conducive to secrecy and (2) it saves the
investigating officer many hours which would otherwise be
spent in canvassing shipping offices, hotels, domestic
utility companies, etc.'

It is now that the work has been in operation for just
under one year that its value is increasing daily and I
suggest for the reasons set forth above that it be continued
for the year 1937.

Its continuation for the coming year will require that
certain modifications be carried out. It will be noticed
by examination of the attached index, which is supplied
with "Leitz" and other similiar files, that the paper is not
sufficiently strong to stand up to continual use, and, that
the visible markings are somewhat small for quick reference.
In this connection I respectfully suggest that a sufficient
number of indices be supplied, constructed of a stronger
material, thus to simplify the work of compilation.

（批：Arrangements have been made with Sims for the supply of more substantial indices. AMR 24/10）

报告。
日期：1936年10月21日。

主题：乘客名单 - 入境与出境。

由刑事调查科副督察长戈尔登（D.S.I. Golder）撰写并呈送。

自1936年1月起实施的将出入境乘客姓名按字母顺序归档至“C.S.6.”分部档案的系统，已被证明对所有需要追踪外国国民出入境情况的人员大有裨益。一旦获得姓名，查询可在不到一分钟内完成，记录中会提供乘客姓名、船名以及抵达或离境日期。

通过上述方式，无需接触外部人员、领事馆或商业机构，即可获取大量宝贵信息，尤其是关于入境者的信息。因此，该系统具有两个显著特点：(1) 更有利于保密；(2) 为调查警官节省了大量原本需花费在走访轮船公司、酒店、公用事业公司等处的时间。

目前该工作运行已近一年，其价值日益凸显。鉴于上述理由，我建议将其延续至1937年。

若要在来年继续实施，需要进行某些修改。通过检查随附的索引（该索引随“Leitz”及其他类似文件夹提供），可以发现纸张强度不足以承受持续使用，且可见标记对于快速查阅而言略显细小。就此，我谨建议提供足够数量的由更坚固材料制成的索引，从而简化编制工作。

（批注：已与西姆斯公司（Sims）安排供应更耐用的索引。助理处长备忘录 10月24日）

The "Leitz" type files used by the section for
the compilation of passengers names during 1936 are still
in good condition and with one or two exception will be
capable of use for the coming year.

One serious fault with the system as it stands
is its comparative incompleteness. For the most part,
the European shipping concerns have rendered the fullest

have stated, when approached, that they would be willing to

by members of this section at regulated intervals.

Such a procedure would greatly facilitate the work

offical recognition, in the form of a letter to the companies
concerned.

REPORT
Date August 24. 1936.

Subject False statement of address in list of dancing partners at
the Vienna Gardens, forwarded to Bubbling Well Station.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Galder.

Relative to the subject matter of the attached report
dated 21.8.36, I have to state as follows :

I visited the Vienna Gardens, Bubbling Well Road, in
the company of a Japanese Detective attached to Bubbling Well
Station and D.S. Kourjansky at 11.30 p.m. on Saturday August 22,
1936. Both the Chinese and Russian managers were interviewed.
The former was informed of the failure of certain of his employees
to give their correct addresses; he promised to have the matter
remedied. It was not practical to obtain a complete list of
dancing partners of the establishment on Saturday last as the
place was crowded and to have called the girls from their clients
would have caused a great deal of inconvenience both to the
management and its patrons.

It was promised that a new and complete list would
be delivered at this office to-day Monday August 24, 1936.
The manager has carried out his promise in so far as the new
list is concerned, but for minor changes it is the same as the
list reaching this office on August 21, 1936, which contained
60 names. The new list contains 75 names but the addresses
have not been changed. The discrepancy in the first list, i.e.
with regard to Machiko and Reiko whose address is given as
No.86 Tsongchow Road remains unchanged in the new list. I
Have satisfied myself that 86 Tsongchow Road is untenanted.

Another matter worthy of note is the manner in which
the names are given. For instance 'Queenie'; any of 10 girls
may answer to such a name in one cabaret. From what can be
observed of the manner in which these lists are being compiled,
it appears that only the barest gesture is being made to comply

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 S. REC. D 8/24
C.S.6, 特别分部. 36
报告
日期：1936年8月24日。

主题：维也纳花园舞厅提交给静安寺路分局的舞伴名单中地址虚假陈述一事。

由刑事调查科副督察长加尔登（D.S.I. Galder）撰写并呈送。

关于附件中日期为1936年8月21日的报告所涉及的事项，我陈述如下：

1936年8月22日星期六晚上11点30分，我与一名隶属于静安寺路分局的日本侦探以及特别分部警司库尔扬斯基（D.S. Kourjansky）一同走访了位于静安寺路的维也纳花园舞厅。我们分别询问了华籍经理和俄籍经理。前者被告知其部分员工未能提供正确地址；他承诺纠正此事。由于上周六该场所拥挤，若将舞女从客人身边叫走会给管理层及其顾客带来极大不便，因此当时无法获取该场所完整的舞伴名单。

对方承诺将于今日，即1936年8月24日星期一，向本处递交一份新的完整名单。经理已履行了关于新名单的承诺，但除了细微变动外，该名单与1936年8月21日送达本处的名单相同，后者包含60个名字。新名单包含75个名字，但地址并未更改。第一份名单中的差异，即关于 Machiko 和 Reiko 的地址列为通州路86号这一情况，在新名单中仍未改变。我已确认通州路86号无人居住。

另一件值得注意的事情是姓名的提供方式。例如“Queenie”；在一家歌舞厅中，可能有10名女孩都叫这个名字。从观察到的这些名单的编制方式来看，似乎只是为了敷衍了事，以符合歌舞厅执照的条件。

犯罪科及特别分部副总监。
（签名）
D. S. I.

FORM NO. 3
G. 40M. 1. 36

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No...........
C.S.6, Special Branch. XXXXXX
REPORT
Date Aug. 21, 1936.

Subject False statement of address in list of dancing partners at the
Vienna Gardens, forwarded to Bubbling Well Station.

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by Em Golden Det.

With reference to the attached list of dancing partners
at the Vienna Gardens, I have to state that the address given
by Machiko and Reiko is false. No.86 Tsongchow Road is now
untenanted, it was previously a boarding house but was closed
on 9th June, 1936.

D. P. S.

D.C. (Crime & Special Branches)

（左侧手写批注：）
C.S.S.
As spoken
det P
22/8

C.S.6, 特別部門。 XXXXXX
報告
日期 1936年8月21日。

事由 關於提交至靜安寺捕房的維也納花園舞廳跳舞伴侶名單中地址虛報一事。

由 偵探處線人 製作 經 黃金 偵探 轉呈

關於附上的維也納花園舞廳跳舞伴侶名單，本人須聲明 Machiko 和 Reiko 所提供的地址為虛假。通州路86號現無人居住，該處此前為寄宿寓所，但已於1936年6月9日關閉。

D. P. S.

副督察長（刑事及特別部門）

（左側手寫批注：）
特別部門秘書
如面諭
偵探 P

REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY 8/24 3 8 36 Date June 18. 1936）
: Subject Hotels --- Failure to keep proper registers --- etc.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. folder.

During routine visits to hotels, both foreign
and Chinese (operated on European lines), carried out during
the past few months, I have been impressed with the general
failure of managers and/or licensees to maintain a proper
register as called for in their licence conditions.
When the attention of hotel clerks and others is
called to the matter they invariably state that it is
impossible for them to obtain the correct names of intending
guests and that were they to insist on such people proving
the statements made in connection with hotel registration
they would be losing a lot of trade.
The matter of hotel registers has been allowed
to fall into disuse, until at present even the better class
hotels do not keep their registers accurate and up to date.
In not a few of the higher class Chinese hotels in Louza
and the Northern Districts, favoured by foreigners for the
purpose of taking their immediate paramours, the registers
are in a deplorable state. More often than not they contain
facetious and sometimes vulgar names, obviously not those
of the persons engaging the rooms.
Experience has shown that this laxity in the
matter of hotel registers often involves the Council in
unnecessary expense when it comes to locating a foreigner
suspected of crime and regarding whom very little is known.
The wanted person by reason of the failure of the licensees to
comply with the terms of their licence, is able to give any
name occurring to him and to thus avoid the attentions of
the Police set to find or watch him. His action often

：主题：旅馆——未能保持适当登记簿——等。
由警佐弗尔德（folder，原文如此，疑为Golder之误）制作并转发。

在过去几个月对中外旅馆（按欧式经营）进行的例行视察中，经理人和/或持照人普遍未能按照其执照条件要求保存适当的登记簿，这一情况令我印象深刻。
当旅馆职员及其他人员被提请注意此事时，他们 invariably（总是）声称，他们无法获得预期客人的正确姓名，如果他们坚持要求这些人证明其在旅馆登记中所作的陈述，他们将失去大量生意。
旅馆登记簿事宜已被放任至荒废地步，以至于目前即使是较高级的旅馆也未将其登记簿保持准确和最新。
在虹口和北区的一些较高级的中式旅馆中，外国人常光顾这些场所以便与其即时情妇幽会，其登记簿状况令人痛心。它们往往包含戏谑甚至有时粗俗的姓名，显然不是入住者的真实姓名。
经验表明，在旅馆登记簿问题上的这种松懈，往往导致公董局在定位涉嫌犯罪且知之甚少的外国人时产生不必要的费用。由于持照人未能遵守执照条款，被通缉者能够随意提供他想到的任何姓名，从而避开警方旨在寻找或监视他的注意力。他的行为往往需要漫长、枯燥且昂贵的调查（如果 p...

Persons connected with the arms, drug and white
slave traffic more often than not put up in hotels as it is
more convenient for them to make sudden moves without
involving themselves in financial losses connected with the
sale of furniture and house fittings, etc. This consideration
is of course not confined to those three divisions of crime;
they are quoted as an example.
Participants in the commission of organized
crime are invariably persons who are provided with a fair
amount of ready cash and are chosen by their leaders because
of their proclivity for mixing with higher class people,
so as to establish themselves socially. Social contacts
are notably easy to make in hotels, it thus becomes necessary
that hotels be given their quota of attention.
Very little can be done in the improvement of
conditions until "Condition 20" of the Hotel Licence is com-
pletely revised, with the phraseology a little more definite
in its terms, especially in its relation to the responsibility
of the licensee. It would of course be necessary that
applicants for accommodation be called upon to prove beyond
reasonable doubt that they were the persons they represented
themselves to be, by the production of their passports or
some other documents of a personal nature. Thus I beg
respectfully to suggest that "Condition 20 of Hotel Licence"
be revised to read somewhat as follows :-
Condition 20
That the licensee keep a permanent

有组织犯罪的参与者 invariably（总是）拥有相当数量的现金，并因其倾向于与上层人士混迹以建立社会地位而被其头目选中。在旅馆中建立社交联系 notably（显著地）容易，因此有必要对旅馆给予应有的关注。
在完全修订“旅馆执照第20条”之前，很难改善现状，其措辞应更加明确，特别是关于持照人的责任部分。当然，有必要要求住宿申请人通过出示护照或其他个人性质的文件，无可置疑地证明他们是其所声称的人。因此，我谨建议将“旅馆执照第20条”修订为大致如下内容：
第20条
持照人应保持永久

display on the reception desk of the hotel.
Should this change be approved the "Registration
Forms" could be collected by the staff of this office each
morning and the resulting information filed as in the manner
for Foreign Lodging Houses. No extra staff would be required
but the addition to the existing information on the matter of
transients would be of tremendous assistance to every branch
of the Force.
I forward herewith a draft form of the
suggested "Registration Form" together with draft forms of
a proposed "Hotel Register", "Daily Departure Sheet", to be
prepared by licensees, and card for filing purposes in

In continuation of my reports on the subject
of foreign lodging houses and the necessity of laying down
a legal definition of same, I submit the following :-
During April 1936, I on two occasions visited
the Licence Office, S.M.C. Revenue Department, on routine
matters pertaining to the operation of Section C.S.6
(Special Branch). On both occasions the question of the
licencing of the "Foreign Lodging House" was discussed.
Since that time I have made careful enquiries of Police
registries, etc., for files bearing on the subject but have
failed to discover anything in the form of a Municipal
Notification or other notice containing a definition of the
term "Lodging House". Not a few opinions have been
rendered as to what should constitute a "Lodging House"
but apparently none of these have ever been put into
practice through legal channels, which fact is clearly
evidenced in Mr. Godfrey Phillips' (Assistant Secretary)
letter to the Deputy Treasurer Revenue dated March 19, 1935,
paragraph 2 of which reads as follows :-
"Since at present the Revenue Office does
"not in practice licence under any fixed
"definition as to what constitutes a lodging
"house, it is thought better for the present
"not to attempt expressly to define what
"constitutes a lodging house for the purpose
"of licencing."
The above decision was made for some very
good reason, there is no doubt, but it leaves the Police
Department in mid air when it comes to the matter of

继此前关于外侨寄宿房屋及制定其法律定义之必要性的报告之后，现提交如下内容：-
1936年4月间，我曾两次因涉及C.S.6科（特别部门）运作的常规事务，前往工部局财政局执照办公室。在这两次访问中，均讨论了“外侨寄宿房屋”的执照颁发问题。自那时起，我曾仔细查阅警务处登记册等档案，寻找与该主题相关的文件，但未能发现任何以工部局通告或其他通知形式存在的、包含“寄宿房屋”一词定义的文件。关于何者应构成“寄宿房屋”，虽有不少意见提出，但显然这些意见从未通过法律途径付诸实施，这一事实明显体现于戈弗雷·菲利普斯先生（助理秘书）于1935年3月19日致财政局副司库的信函中，该信第二段内容如下：-
“鉴于目前财政局在实际操作中并未依据任何固定的‘寄宿房屋’构成定义来颁发执照，故认为暂时不宜尝试明确界定何为出于执照颁发目的的‘寄宿房屋’。”
上述决定无疑有其充分理由，但这使得警务处在处理相关事务时处于无所适从的境地

（左侧手写批注：f.j. 1936年7月21日）

The Council under Byelaw 34, as explained
by Mr. Phillips, has every legal right to licence lodging
houses and has in the past exercised that right
with no uncertainty without, except in one or two obscure
cases, taking the matter into court. At present, however,
there is to be observed a pronounced difference in the
attitude of the would be boarding house keeper.
Of late not a few persons, operating what
for example, under British Law would be termed lodging
houses, have failed to obtain licences from the S.M.C.
In one case, that of Mrs. Rutherford of No.5 Yang Terrace,
Weihaiwei Road, the opinion of the Municipal Legal
Department was sought, and although not less than seven
persons (lodgers without board) were residing in the house
in question, it was considered that the case would fail if
taken to Court. In the initial stages of the investigation
the assistance of Mr. Feltham Watson, U.S. District
Attorney, was sought. He suggested that the Police should
deal with the case through Mr. Stanton also of the U.S.
Consulate. This gentleman when interviewed was rather
insistant on obtaining the local or Municipal definition
of a Lodging House so that should the case be brought
before the Court the offence committed under Byelaw 34
could be defined. Lacking such definition the case was
not pressed.
In not a few cases occuring since I have
been in charge of C.S.6 it has been necessary for the
staff of the section to spend weeks cajoling the unlicenced

正如菲利普斯先生（Mr. Phillips）所解释，工部局根据附则第34条，拥有颁发寄宿房屋执照的充分法律权利，且过去在行使该权利时毫不迟疑，除了一两起晦涩不明的案件外，并未将此类事项诉诸法庭。然而，目前可以观察到，有意经营寄宿房屋者的态度出现了显著差异。
近来，不少经营着按英国法律可称为寄宿房屋的场所的人士，未能从上海工部局获得执照。在其中一例，即威海卫路杨台5号鲁瑟福夫人（Mrs. Rutherford）一案中，曾征询工部局法律处的意见，尽管涉案房屋内居住着不少于七名人员（不含膳食的房客），但认为若将此案诉诸法庭，将会败诉。在调查初期，曾寻求美国地区检察官费尔瑟姆·沃森先生（Mr. Feltham Watson）的协助。他建议警方通过同样来自美国领事馆的斯坦顿先生（Mr. Stanton）处理此案。这位先生在面谈时，坚持要求获得关于“寄宿房屋”的地方性或工部局定义，以便若案件被提交法庭，能够明确界定违反附则第34条的罪行。由于缺乏此类定义，该案未予追究。
自本人负责中央巡捕房第六区（C.S.6）以来，在发生的不少案件中，该区职员不得不花费数周时间劝说无照经营者

particular officers time and placing upon him an

has been hampered to no uncertain degree in its normal
function of collecting information on the movements of
undesirables etc. Such work in a city of the importance
of Shanghai is of no small account and although it is not
within the sphere of any Police force to unduly interfere

out. Discretion, of course, is exercised in the matter
of visiting boarding houses, those which are to be
considered respectable or of the higher class are not
given the attention of those known to house persons of
ill repute or operated by such.

    Nevertheless, it has been proved during the
past three months that a careful co-ordination of information
gathered from licenced premises, of the description under
report, has had a very desirable effect. No less than
89 reports on the movements of convicted persons and/or
suspects have been submitted and two persons arrested and
successfully prosecuted for criminal offences.

    To-date there are many persons, chiefly in
the Eastern District of Shanghai (International Settlement)
operating small unlicenced boarding houses of fairly low
class and it is in such places that the fugitive, foolish
enough to remain in Shanghai after the commission of an
offence, is to be found. The licencing of such premises
coupled with the complete co-operation with the French

Subject Boarding Houses --- Failure of Licensees to Keep Proper Registers.

There has been evidence of late of the failure on
the part of lower class boarding house keepers to maintain
a proper register of guests in their houses.
In connection with this matter I request permission
to introduce a system of notifications similar in purpose to
those used by the Traffic Department. Such notices could
be typed and numbered and delivered by the Foreign Detectives
at the time of their normal visits, thus avoiding any
appreciable expense and obviating the necessity for extra staff.

The notices could take the form :

*Name Notification No.1
*Address " " 2
"Dear Sir/Madame.
"I have to draw your attention to Condition 2
*of Boarding and/or Lodging House Licence issued
*to you by the S. M. C., which provides that you
*must at all times maintain a proper register of
*persons residing in the premises of which you
*are the licensee."

Duplicates of the notices would be kept in this
office and would be of use as evidence in cases where
licensees were prosecuted, say after two such notifications
had been ignored.

D. S. I.

Date...January 3, 1936.
(印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE File No. S. B. D. 8/24 Section 36)

Subject...Boarding House Registers --- Purchase and cost of printing ---
Sale to boarding house operators.
Made by...and....................................................Forwarded by...........D.S.I. Golder.

On December 15, 1935, Mr. Volsky, Office Assistant,
attached to C.S.6, approached me with regard to the registers
supplied to the operators of boarding houses, as it had become
necessary to purchase a fresh supply. He explained that for
the past 2½ years he had arranged for the private purchase
of the books and recovered his money as they were sold to
licence holders. Such a system of supplying an article laid
down in police regulations as being necessary in compliance
with licence conditions appears to be unsatisfactory and capable
of placing a hardship upon the person providing them, since he
is compelled to pay cash and only retrieves his money a dollar
or so at a time.

As an alternative, I respectfully suggest that the
printing be placed in the hands of the Stationery Office and
that the outlay be classified as "Recoverable Expenditure",
since the licence holders are called upon to pay for the registers.

Another aspect is, that, unless the practice of
making the licence holders purchase the "registers" is continued
they will become careless of their maintenance.

Attached to this report will be found an old register
as a sample of what is required together with a revised layout
of the items of information required. The personal particulars
of boarders in the revised form are grouped as they naturally
would occur to the persons called upon to compile them.

For the year ending December 1936 something in the
region of 60 registers will be needed at an average cost of
$1.20 each.

Another matter which I respectfully wish to bring
to notice is the time expended on the examination of registers.

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处档案号 S. B. D. 8/24 第36节）

事由……寄宿公寓登记簿——印刷采购及成本——向寄宿公寓经营者出售。
呈报人……及………………………………………转呈人……副督察长 Golder。

1935年12月15日，隶属中央捕房特别股的办公室助理 Volsky 先生就供应给寄宿公寓经营者的登记簿一事与我接洽，因为有必要采购新一批登记簿。他解释说，在过去两年半的时间里，他一直安排私下购买这些登记簿，并在将其出售给执照持有人时收回款项。这种供应方式涉及警务规章中规定为遵守执照条件所必需的物品，似乎并不令人满意，且可能给提供者带来困难，因为他被迫支付现金，而每次只能收回一美元左右的款项。

作为替代方案，我谨建议将印刷工作交由文书科（Stationery Office）负责，并将此项支出归类为“可收回支出”，因为执照持有人需付费购买登记簿。

另一方面，除非继续要求执照持有人购买“登记簿”，否则他们可能会疏于对登记簿的维护。

本报告附有一份旧登记簿作为所需样式的样本，以及经修订的所需信息项目排版。修订后表格中的住客个人详细信息已按照编制人员自然想到的顺序进行分组。

截至1936年12月的一年内，大约需要60本登记簿，平均每本成本为1.20元。

C.S.6, Special Branch x-36
REPORT
Date... January 22, 1936.
Subject Shipping --- Passenger Lists Supplied by Chinese Passport Office ---
Suggestions for Simplification of Reference --- Arrivals & Departures.
Made by/... and ... Forwarded by ... D.S.I. Jolder.

In the pursuance of enquiries into the movements,
etc., of criminals, criminal suspects, persons suspected of
undesirable political activity and those persons regarding
whom the Police are from time to time requested to report
on, it is invariably necessary to establish (A) the date of
his/her arrival in Shanghai, (B) Port of Embarkation, (C)
the name of the vessel on which subject travelled, and (D)
the reference given to the passport authorities on arrival.
Vice versa, in the matter of departures, the points from
which an enquiry would of necessity start would be (A) date
of departure, (B) name of vessel, and (C) Destination.
Section C.S.6 is in receipt of passenger lists
(in-coming) from the Chinese Passport Office. These are
listed according to companies and in chronological order.
Despite this it invariably happens that no particulars can
be offered regarding the subject of an enquiry other than
a name. Such being the case, and there being no indication
as to the date of arrival, it becomes necessary for the
investigating officer to start reading carefully through
some 16 files, each containing some 250 pages, bearing an
average of 20 names each. Unless a certain amount of luck
attends the search, it might, as has been the case, after
other methods have failed, be necessary to go through the
whole list, a business sometimes taking as long as two days
and at least a number of hours.
To avoid such waste of time it is suggested
that the lists as supplied by the Chinese Passport Authorities
and the lists of departures which are obtained from various
sources be put up in alphabetical order using at least a

主题 航运 --- 由中国护照办公室提供的乘客名单 --- 简化查阅的建议 --- 抵达与离境。
制作人/... 及 ... 转呈人 ... 副督察长 Jolder。

为了追查罪犯、犯罪嫌疑人、涉嫌从事不良政治活动者以及警方不时被要求报告其情况的人员的行踪等， invariably（总是）有必要确定 (A) 其抵达上海的日期，(B) 登船港口，(C) 当事人乘坐的船只名称，以及 (D) 抵达时向护照当局提供的参考编号。反之，在离境事项中，调查必然起始于 (A) 离境日期，(B) 船只名称，以及 (C) 目的地。
C.S.6 科收到来自中国护照办公室的乘客名单（入境）。这些名单按公司分类并按时间顺序排列。尽管如此， invariably（总是）会出现除了姓名之外，无法提供关于调查对象的任何详细信息的情况。既然情况如此，且没有抵达日期的指示，负责调查的警官就必须开始仔细翻阅大约16个档案卷，每卷包含约250页，平均每页有20个名字。除非搜索过程中有一定的运气，否则正如已经发生的那样，在其他方法失败后，可能需要通读整个名单，这项工作有时长达两天，至少也需要数小时。
为避免此类时间浪费，建议将由中方护照当局提供的名单以及从各种来源获得的离境名单，使用至少四个字母的参考编号，按字母顺序排列。

June 3, 1935.
No. D 8/24
Date 6 / 6 / 35

A/ Commissioner of Police.

Sir,

Proposed Changes in Special Branch.

In order to relieve congestion in the offices of the
Special Branch in the new building, it will be necessary to
transfer the Boarding-House Section to the office originally
intended for Film Censorship and to divide the staff of the
latter section between the Translators' Bureau and the Registry
in both of which offices there is some vacant space.

The Boarding-House Section will then be on the 3rd
floor and the Indian Section on the 2nd floor. I propose,
subject to your approval, to place these two sections under the
same officer.

This arrangement will increase the efficiency of S.2 as
the section specially intended for dealing with Communist
matters, and will not interfere with the efficiency of the
Boarding-House Section or its usefulness to D.C.(Crime) and
the Special Branch.

The efficiency of S.2 will be increased by relieving
the officer in charge of S.2 of miscellaneous duties not
strictly within his province, such as inquiries regarding
applicants for licences, locating of people lost, checking &
records of applicants to join S.V.C. Russian Unit, etc., etc.

The efficiency of S.2 will be maintained because
D.S. Sansom will remain in immediate charge under D.S.I.Golden.
Both of these officers have had several years' experience
in the Crime Branch and Special Branch.

Subject to your approval, I shall also endeavour to find
a formula whereby Supt. Tah, in addition to his liaison duties,
will take a share in the responsibility for the loyalty and
general good behaviour of the Chinese staff of the Special
Branch.

J.M.
D.C.(Sp.Br.).

(批：Copy made for file S 8/50)
(批：Re. S. Kile)

日期 35年6月6日

致 警务总监。

先生，

特别处的拟议变更。

为了缓解新大楼内特别处办公室的拥挤状况，有必要将寄宿公寓科迁至原定为电影审查使用的办公室，并将该科的人员分配至翻译股和档案室，这两个办公室均有一些空闲空间。

此后，寄宿公寓科将位于三楼，印度人科位于二楼。我建议，在您批准的前提下，将这两个科置于同一名官员的管理之下。

这一安排将提高专门处理共产主义事务的 S.2 科的效率，并且不会干扰寄宿公寓科的效率或其对犯罪科副处长和特别处的效用。

通过免除 S.2 科主管不属于其严格职权范围内的杂务，如有关执照申请人的查询、寻找失踪人员、核查并记录加入义勇军俄罗斯分队的申请人等，S.2 科的效率将得到提高。

由于 D.S. Sansom 将在 D.S.I. Golden 的直接领导下继续负责，S.2 科的效率将得以维持。这两名官员在犯罪科和特别处都有多年的经验。

在您批准的前提下，我还将努力寻找一种方案，使 Tah 巡官除了履行联络职责外，还能分担特别处华员员工的忠诚度及一般良好行为的责任。

J.M.
特别处副处长。

(批：为档案 S 8/50 制作副本)
(批：关于 S. Kile)

the Boarding House Section was transferred to the Special
Branch, Section 2, as the first move in a plan to centralize
all information in regard to foreign criminals. The follow-
ing is a summary of the work undertaken by the personnel of
the Boarding House Section showing the progress made between
June 1 and October 31:-

(1) Record cards giving full particulars, where available,
have been prepared of 731 criminals, 657 suspected
criminals and 351 individuals wanted by police authorities
other than the Municipal Police for offences committed
in their territories. For the time being these record
cards are filed in alphabetical order under the respective
headings "Criminals," "Suspects A" and "Suspects B."
Providing the approval of the Deputy Commissioner,
Special Branch, is obtained, however, it is proposed to
cross-index all records at an early date. This method of
filing is superior in many ways to the present system of
single alphabetical filing and the alteration could be
made with material already at our disposal.

(2) 2548 visits have been paid to boarding-houses and 68
visits to hotels, bars, cafes and cabarets. 20 appli-
cations for boarding-house licences and 37 applications
for miscellaneous licences have been attended to.

(3) 54 reports regarding the movements of old criminals and
16 reports on the activities of new criminal suspects
have been submitted.

呈报人：督察长 Everest 转呈人：（签名） 督察长

根据1934年5月16日第C.8488号警务命令，寄宿公寓股于1934年6月1日划归特务科第二科，作为集中所有有关外籍罪犯信息计划的第一步。以下是寄宿公寓股人员开展工作的摘要，显示了6月1日至10月31日期间取得的进展：-

(1) 已为731名罪犯、657名嫌疑犯以及351名因在其辖区内犯罪而被非工部局警务处的警察当局通缉的个人编制了记录卡，在资料可得的情况下提供了详尽细节。目前，这些记录卡按字母顺序分别归档在“罪犯”、“A类嫌疑犯”和“B类嫌疑犯”标题下。然而，一旦获得特务科副总监的批准，拟尽早对所有记录进行交叉索引。这种归档方法在许多方面优于目前的单一字母顺序归档系统，且利用我们现有的材料即可进行更改。

(2) 已对寄宿公寓进行了2548次走访，对旅馆、酒吧、咖啡馆和歌舞厅进行了68次走访。处理了20份寄宿公寓执照申请和37份杂项执照申请。

C.S.2.
June 7, 1934.

D. Chelmis.

Made by D.I. Schmidt Forwarded by D.I. Ross.

Sir,

Last month (May) the Revenue Department informed Police Headquarters that House 46, Lane 41, Carter Road, was operated as a boarding house without a licence.

The undersigned made inquiries at the address mentioned and was assured by the occupier a Mr. D. Chelmis, Greek, that his house was not a boarding house, having only four friends, countrymen of his, residing there, but was also informed that he might open a boarding house in June.

Mr. D. Chelmis was again interviewed by the undersigned this morning, June 7, when, he, Chelmis claimed that only unfurnished rooms and small flats were sublet, and that at present he had seven persons residing on the premises, two married couples and three single men. These people supplied their own furniture and their own meals, and therefore he (Mr. Chelmis) was of the opinion that his premises should not be classed as a boarding house or lodging house, but should be classified as an apartment house (apartment houses are not licenced).

There are at present about 284 licenced boarding houses, but this is the first instance that such a question has arisen and it would be useful if some ruling on the difference between lodging houses and apartment houses could be had for future reference.

Yours obediently,

Officer i/c Special Branch.

Subject (in full) Criminal Shelter at I Boundary Lane.

Made by D.S. Ovsiannikoff. Forwarded by J.M. Evens A.C. Pol.

I beg to report that a boarding house kept by a man known by the nickname of "Volodka Greek" at I Boundary Lane in Chinese territory is a rendez-vous for local Russian criminals mostly pickpockets and shoplifters.

"Volodka Greek" sublets rooms to the criminals of various class and also collects revenues from these criminals and their associates for permitting them to gamble on his premises. The following criminals are residing in the house at the present time:-

Mr. Volodka Greek Tenant. Receiver of stolen property and swindler.
Mr. L. Roojansky Expert pickpocket
Mr. N. Fox alias Fuchs Expert pickpocket.
Mr. A. Rosenbaum Expert pickpocket.

(C.I.D.) Office Notes

January 18, 1929

A/D.C.I.

As a result of the work of the Foreign Section in
connection with the collection of boarding house lists it has
been ascertained that information concerning known and/or
suspected foreign criminals and addresses frequented by them is
now available. In order therefore to utilise this intelligence
for the benefit of the C.I.D. I beg to suggest that two lists
as per attached draft: 1 "List of Known and/or Suspected
Foreign Criminals Residing in Shanghai" and 2 "List of
Foreign Boarding or Lodging Houses Frequented by Known and/or
Suspected Foreign Criminals" be issued monthly, or at whatever
intervals as may meet with your approval, to Senior detectives.

List No.1 would contain the name, address and brief summary
of the antecedents of the person mentioned and would enable for-
eign detectives to keep in touch with the movements of the
foreign criminal element.

List No 2 would contain the names of the tenant and addresses
of foreign boarding houses ( principally Russian ) frequented by
certain classes of criminals and would assist foreign detectives
in cases where considerable property is stolen to arrive at a
possible conclusion as to where the property might be concealed.

The information contained in these lists would be verified,
as far as possible by further inquiries and by reference to the
Finger Print Bureau for criminal records. They would then be
compiled by the Officer I/C Foreign Section and forwarded in
the usual manner. Mimeograph copies would then have to be made
for distribution to stations and should be treated strictly
confidential.

由于外籍科在收集寄宿公寓名单方面的工作，现已查明有关已知和/或疑似外籍罪犯及其经常光顾的地址的信息。因此，为了利用这些情报以利于刑事侦缉处，谨建议按照附上的草稿印发两份名单：1 “居住在上海的已知和/或疑似外籍罪犯名单” 和 2 “已知和/或疑似外籍罪犯经常光顾的外籍寄宿或寄宿舍名单”，每月或以您批准的任何间隔时间发给高级侦探。

名单第1号将包含提及人员的姓名、地址和前科简要摘要，使外籍侦探能够掌握外籍犯罪分子的动向。

名单第2号将包含某些类别罪犯经常光顾的外籍寄宿公寓（主要是俄国人）的租户姓名和地址，这将协助外籍侦探在发生大量财产被盗的案件中，就可能隐藏财产的地点得出初步结论。

这些名单中包含的信息将通过进一步调查和查阅指纹局的犯罪记录尽可能进行核实。然后由外籍科主管警官编制并按常规方式转发。随后需制作油印副本分发给各分局，并应严格作为机密处理。

File No. 108569
(C.I.D.) Office Notes
May 25, 1925

D.C.I.

With the transfer of P.C.S.Makaroff, P.C.C.Suhoff and
P.C.G.Kedvedeff to the Foreign Section sufficient Russian
staff is now available to complete the number of Russian
detectives required for boarding house work without having
to transfer any additional men from Stations. Two British
detectives, however, are required to complete the personnel
as agreed upon at the conference held in the office of the
Director of Criminal Investigation on March 25, 1925.

The distribution will then be:-
"A" Div. One British and two Russian detectives.
"B" " One " " one " detective.

Drafts of the duties to be performed by the British and
Russian detectives are attached for your approval.

T.P.C. Braikovsky will operate the Russian Boarding
House filing system.

The space required, however, is not yet available and in
order to bring the scheme to realisation it is hoped that
the additional space will be found as soon as possible. The
furniture agreed upon, with the exception of the filing
cabinet which has been obtained, is also urgently required.

As a consequence of the work of the Boarding House
Section it is hoped that the Foreign Section will be able to
supply at regular periods lists of known criminal or political
suspects or known offenders which will greatly assist in
keeping station detectives in touch with the location and
the movements of these undesirables.

Ruy

A. Robertson

See C.R.A. 9700 How does the accommodation
question now stand? 2/6/25

C D J Gilbert
20/6/25 Mr Stallybrass states matter is pending he
has sent to Finance Dept this after Secretary

1925年5月25日

刑事侦缉处处长

随着警员 Makaroff、警员 Suhoff 和
警员 G. Kedvedeff 调至外事科，目前已有足够的俄籍
职员来补足寄宿屋工作所需的俄籍
侦探人数，而无需从各巡捕房抽调更多人员。然而，仍需两名英籍
侦探以补足 personnel，正如1925年3月25日在
刑事侦缉处处长办公室举行的会议上所商定。

届时人员分配如下：-
“A”区：一名英籍和两名俄籍侦探。
“B”区：一名英籍和一名俄籍侦探。

英籍和俄籍侦探的职责草案已附上，供 阁下批准。

T.P.C. Braikovsky 将负责运作俄籍公寓
档案系统。

然而，所需空间目前尚未到位，为了
使该计划得以实现，希望能尽快找到
额外空间。除已获得的文件柜外，商定的
家具也急需到位。

鉴于寄宿屋科的工作，希望外事科能够
定期提供已知罪犯或政治嫌疑分子或已知
违法者的名单，这将极大地协助各巡捕房
侦探掌握这些不受欢迎者的行踪和
动向。

Ruy

pages.en:
Duties of Senior (British) Detective on
Boarding House Section.
------------------------

To, visit all British and American boarding houses once
every week and obtain from each house weekly a list giving
the nationality, occupation, place of employment, last address,
destination and date of arrival and departure of all persons
resorting to or using the premises and to bring such lists to
headquarters for the use of the Boarding House Registry.

To supervise the work of the Russian Boarding House
Detective working in the same division by periodically visiting
the Russian Boarding Houses to check signatures, visits, etc.etc.

To remember that no meeting of a political nature or at
which any address or discussion on politics is allowed, nor
any meeting or distribution of inflammatory, obscene or other
literature which may cause a breech of the peace and good order
of the Settlement, be permitted in or upon any part of the
premises without the written sanction of the Council first
had and obtained.

To report any disorderly or immoral conduct or gambling
in or upon any part of the premises to the Station of the
District concerned and to the officer in charge of the
"Foreign Section" of the Intelligence Branch.

To report every morning at the office of the Foreign
Section before starting work and to report every evening half
an hour before the official closing hour with the boarding house
slips collected during the day.

To locate all political or criminal suspects or known
offenders (as they come to his knowledge) using foreign boarding
houses and to report their presence as soon as possible to the
officer in charge of the Foreign Section.

寄宿屋科高级（英籍）侦探职责。
------------------------

每周走访所有英籍和美籍公寓一次，并从每家公寓每周获取一份名单，列明所有光顾或使用该房产人员的国籍、职业、工作地点、最后住址、目的地以及抵达和离开日期，并将此类名单带回总部，供寄宿屋档案室使用。

通过定期走访俄籍公寓以核对签名、访问记录等，监督在同一辖区工作的俄籍公寓侦探的工作。

切记，未经工部局事先获得书面批准，不得在任何房产的任何部分允许举行任何具有政治性质的会议，或允许发表任何政治演说或进行政治讨论，也不得允许举行任何会议或分发可能引起破坏租界和平与良好秩序的煽动性、淫秽或其他文献。

向相关辖区巡捕房及情报分支外事科主管警官报告任何房产内发生的扰乱秩序或不道德行为或赌博活动。

每天开始工作前向外事科办公室报到，并在每天官方下班时间前半小时携带当天收集的公寓单据进行汇报。

查明所有使用外籍公寓的政治或刑事嫌疑分子或已知违法者（在其知晓范围内），并尽快向外事科主管警官报告其存在。

File No. 10. 8569
February 21, 1928

D. C. I. . .

With reference to your recent instructions
re the more stringent supervision of Russian
and other foreign boarding houses, I beg
to submit the following proposals, which,
it is hoped, will meet all requirements.

In order to obtain satisfactory results
it is proposed to combine boarding houses,
low class hotels and cafes, principally
Russian.

Supervision & Distribution

It is proposed to divide the Internation-
al Settlement into three sub-divisions, which
will bring about the even distribution of
the number of premises to be visited, viz
(1) Hongkew and West Hongkew Districts
(2) Wayside and Yangtzepoo Districts
(3) Harbin Road, Dixwell Road, Gordon Road
Pootoo Road, Bubblingwell, Sinza House
and Central Districts.

One Russian detective would then
be allotted to each sub-division and his
duties would be to visit every boarding
house and low class hotel once every
week, to check the register kept on these
premises, to collect a written list of resident
guests and to bring such list to Headquarters
for inclusion in the Boarding house Registry.
It would also be the duty of the officer
of the Sub-division to locate all unlicensed
boarding houses in his district and to re-
port the existence of such to Holgers.

He would also be responsible for
providing information regarding the names
of cafes, their proprietors; and the means
pages.zh:
（刑事调查处）办公室备忘录
档案号 10. 8569
1928年2月21日

副总巡……

关于阁下近期就加强对俄罗斯人及其他外国人经营的寄宿公寓进行更严格监管的指示，谨呈上以下建议，希望能满足各项要求。

为了取得令人满意的效果，建议将寄宿公寓、低档旅馆和咖啡馆（主要为俄罗斯人经营）合并管理。

监管与分区

建议将公共租界划分为三个分区，以便均衡分配需巡查的场所数量，即：
(1) 虹口及西虹口区
(2) 韦尔斯利路区（Wayside）及杨树浦区
(3) 哈尔滨路、狄思威路、戈登路、普陀路、静安寺、新闸路及中央区。

每个分区将指派一名俄籍侦探，其职责为每周巡查辖区内每一家寄宿公寓和低档旅馆一次，核查这些场所保存的登记簿，收集住客书面名单，并将该名单带回总部，录入寄宿公寓登记册。该分区警官的另一项职责是查明辖区内所有无照经营的寄宿公寓，并向霍尔格斯（Holgers）报告此类情况的存在。

他还负责提供有关咖啡馆名称、业主及其经营方式的信息

pages.en:
in which these places are conducted
Boarding House Registry
It is proposed to eliminate the present
system of book records and to institute
a correct filing system whereby every guest
will be included in a special card
giving his particulars and antecedents, the
idea being to have a complete record of
each individual in a separate document
which will be always up-to-date.
Prosecutions
It is proposed that the Foreign Section,
or whatever body is designated to do the work
will not actually undertake the entire
work in connection with prosecutions and
it is suggested that applications for
summons will be made from Algiers
but will be served by the station of
the district concerned who will like-
wise enter the offence in the charge sheet
and present the case at Court; the officer
concerned need then only appear to give
evidence. This will obviate the necessity
of a special Chinese staff being employed
and will save the time of a foreign
officer serving a summons when that
duty can be easily executed by a
Chinese member of the Force.
Staff
It is proposed that the staff necessary
to carry out this work will be four
officers under the control of the officer
in charge of the Foreign Section. They
will be distributed as follows:
pages.zh:
寄宿公寓登记册
建议取消目前的簿记制度，建立一套正确的归档系统，使每位客人都列入一张专门的卡片，记录其个人详情及背景，旨在为每个人建立一份始终最新的独立完整档案。
起诉
建议由外事组或指定负责此项工作的机构不实际承担与起诉相关的全部工作；建议传票申请由阿尔及尔（Algiers）（注：此处原文疑为笔误，可能指代某部门或人员，照译）提出，但由相关辖区的巡捕房送达，该巡捕房同样需在控罪书上登记罪行并在法庭出庭陈述案情；有关警官只需出庭作证即可。这将避免雇佣专门的中方职员的需要，并节省外籍警官送达传票的时间，因为该项任务可由警队中的华籍成员轻松执行。
人员配置
建议执行此项工作所需的人员为四名警官，受外事组主管警官指挥。具体分配如下：

Sir,
I suggest the following procedure be adopted
to avoid unnecessary delay in dealing with applications
for boarding-house licenses :
(1) A foot-note reading as follows be printed on the
copies of applications sent to Departments : "This
application form must be returned completed to the
Commissioner of Revenue within five days of issue.
(2) After a license has been approved for issue, or
refused, the applicant be immediately notified in
writing by the Revenue. Dept. A small printed form
would serve this purpose and as there are only five
or six applications monthly, very little work or
expense would be entailed if the notification was sent
by post.
This would ensure that within ten days,
applications are adequately dealt with. Senior detectives
i/c of Districts could be notified of licenses refused and
the reasons for refusal. If, then, within a reasonable
period of time, commensurate with the work to be done,
applicant did not effect the necessary changes, and
persisted in using the premises as a boarding-house, he,
or she, could be dealt with on summons.
